name: EGYPT

lead: Egypt sits in Africa and Asia. The Nile river turns desert into farmland. Pyramids built 4,500 years ago are as tall as a 48-storey building. Egypt has more people than any other Arab (Arabic-speaking) country.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Egypt is 96% desert. A narrow green ribbon along the Nile is 5% of the land, yet almost everyone lives there. The Nile flows 6,650 km north to the Mediterranean.
The Sinai Peninsula links Africa to Asia. The Suez Canal cuts the northeast, so ships save weeks skipping the trip around Africa.
animals: Ancient Egyptians worshipped the Nile crocodile as the god Sobek. It can reach 6 metres. Millions of sacred ibis birds were mummified as gifts for Thoth, god of wisdom.
The fennec fox has huge ears that release body heat. Scarab beetles roll dung into balls. Ancient Egyptians saw them as a sign of new life.
culture: Egyptians are warm hosts. Refusing a second helping is almost unthinkable! Ful medames (slow-cooked fava beans) and koshari are daily meals. Koshari mixes lentils, rice, pasta and tomato sauce.
In Ramadan, glowing lanterns called fanous light up the streets. Families share iftar, the meal that ends each day's fast. Looping Arabic writing decorates mosques and wedding cards.
history: Egypt's first pharaoh united the country around 3100 BCE. Pharaohs ruled for 3,000 years. The Great Pyramid was Earth's tallest building for nearly 4,000 years.
Greek, Roman, Arab, Turkish (Ottoman) and British rulers all came later. The Arab conquest in 641 CE brought Islam and Arabic. Egypt became independent in 1952.
wows: The Great Pyramid holds enough stone to build a wall around France.
Ancient Egyptians invented the 365-day calendar over 5,000 years ago.
Cairo's metro is Africa's oldest subway, carrying over 3.5 million riders a day.
More ancient obelisks (tall stone pillars) stand in Rome than in all of Egypt.
The Nile Delta, the river's fan-shaped end, was built entirely from Ethiopian Highlands mud.
Tutankhamun, Egypt's famous boy king, became pharaoh at just nine years old.
Egypt grows over 2 million tonnes of dates a year, more than any other country.
